A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, algorithms, experiments, and Appendices A–C. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report original model-retraining experiments on Adult, Folktables ACSEmployment, and HMDA, including marginal-gain, accuracy, disparate-impact, and miscoverage results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the original model-retraining experiments and their empirical results. These qualify as original results even though they are unchanged from v1.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2, their stopping conditions, and their conditional expected improvement bounds are unchanged. V2's explanation of accuracy-thresholded sampling describes a procedure already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Adult income prediction, Folktables ACSEmployment for Alabama in 2018, and HMDA mortgage origination for New York in 2017. Appendix A confirms unchanged tasks, populations, and protected/reference groups.

E2.justification: The full-information reference and comparisons involving Algorithms 1 and 2 are retained. Figures 2, 4, and 5 use the same vanilla and Fairlearn versions of logistic regression, random forests, and gradient boosted trees.

E3.justification: The semisynthetic evaluation design, 3,000-point sampled datasets, 5,000-model pools, 100-iteration trajectories, and failure probability of 0.05 remain unchanged. No evaluation metric, preprocessing procedure, or experimental configuration is revised.

E4.justification: The CEI-estimation comparison, Fairlearn sensitivity discussion, and finite-/infinite-data miscoverage and selection-effect diagnostics are retained. Appendix A and Figures 4 and 8–10 contain no added or removed analyses.

E5.justification: Both report 45 dataset repetitions, 5,000 bootstrapped trajectories per dataset repetition, and the same standard-deviation shading and parenthesized summaries. No uncertainty-reporting practice or repeated-run information is added or revised.

E6.justification: The plotted graphics and all numerical entries in Figures 6–8 are unchanged. For example, Folktables random-forest miscoverage remains 0.381 without Fairlearn and 0.484 with Fairlearn in Figure 8. No measured results are added or removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, formal results, and proofs in Appendices B–C are unchanged. V2 adds informal commentary around Lemma 3.2 without revising its statement, bound, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its description of empirical validation from credit, employment, and housing to credit and housing, although the employment experiment remains. The central adaptive-stopping and statistical-guarantee contributions are retained.

C2.justification: V2 connects accuracy-constrained search explicitly to legal business needs and qualifies extensions to data/feature decisions as requiring a sampling formulation. It also adds interpretations of Lemma 3.2 and Figure 2, including an incorrect description of the probability bound as bounding the running minimum and an unsupported inference of polynomial decay from the logarithmic vertical axis. Existing miscoverage explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Dataset preparation, model defaults, random-forest settings, Fairlearn parameters, hardware, training-time and cost disclosures, and the code-access link are unchanged. No new implementation or reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds HUD's 2020 and 2023 regulatory documents and uses them to expand the legal motivation concerning acceptable LDA-search costs. The technical related-work positioning is retained; several other reference edits update publication metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract, expands and reorganizes the introduction, moves existing scope discussion from Section 5 into the introduction, and places the Pandora's Box discussion under related work. Local explanations, bibliographic cleanup, and the repaired Appendix A figure reference accompany these changes; the overall technical structure remains intact.

P2.justification: All figures and tables retain their graphics and table structures. Figure 2's caption gains an explanation of its logarithmic scale, while Table 1 and several appendix floats shift relative to surrounding prose, producing limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the legal framing and repairs a broken figure reference, but introduces inaccuracies in technical exposition. Section 3.2 describes Lemma 3.2 as bounding the running minimum, although its unchanged statement bounds the probability of a new minimum; Appendix B uses a uniform transformation to connect these quantities. Section 4 and Figure 2 also infer polynomial decay from a logarithmic vertical axis alone. These misleading additions outweigh the limited editorial gains, while the formal results and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
